graphEvents.label: What registering a new sk-code mode requires
Registry, routerSignals and leaf-manifest move in lockstep

label: The sk-code router compiler dereferences hubRouter.routerSignals[workflowMode].classes and .weight with no guard, so a mode registered only in mode-registry.json fails the compile instead of scoring zero.

tieBreak is checked three ways: 5e exact permutation of registry modes, 5i workflow modes before non-workflow, 5l no added surface after the native surface; a new mode is inserted at a constrained index determined by its packetKind.

leaf-manifest.json is generated by generate-leaf-manifest.cjs and re-validated by parent-skill-check (10a-manifest-source), so hand-editing it is the one act that yields a green registry with a stale inventory.

Only workflowMode and backendKind are hard FAIL fields on a mode entry (3d); packetKind, packetSkillName, grandfatheredFolderMismatch, aliases and toolSurface are softFail, so a malformed mode degrades the gate to a warning.

A surface packet is contractually read-only and advisor-invisible: 3g forces backendKind evidence-base, routingClass metadata, mutatesWorkspace:false, allowed subset of {Read,Bash,Grep,Glob} and a forbidden list covering the mutating tools.
Adding a mode touches 11 integration surfaces but only rows 1-3, 7 (name only) and 9 are gated; rows 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 have no gate, so a green per-hub gate does not prove a mode is reachable.

verify-router-sync leg 3 asserts compiled destinations, leaf-manifest.json and the code-skilled RESOURCE_MAP agree through qualifiedIdToLeaf, so a mode with leaves also edits root ROUTER.md and the guard checks the union.
sk-code declares only the surface-axis extension, so a new mode in this hub needs no runtimeLoopType; that field is enforced only where the runtime-loop extension is declared.

sk-code-ci cannot be a read-only surface if it scaffolds workflows: the standards half fits a surface, the scaffolding half must be a command or a workflow mode with mutatesWorkspace:true. Which half owns /doctor:ci remains UNKNOWN.
Registration is a roughly 9-file act; the only authoring command the checker names is /create:skill-parent update --surfaces, which covers surface placement only.

direction: Register sk-code-ci as a surface packet and let it scaffold workflows from there
reason: A surface packet is contractually read-only and advisor-invisible (3g), so it cannot mutate workflow YAML; the scaffolding half needs a command or a workflow mode.
